Flux of Isotropic Radiation • Total flux: Fν = Fν⁺ − Fν⁻;  Fν = ∫ Iν cosθ dΩ = Iν ∫ cosθ sinθ dθ dφ = 2πIν ∫ sinθ cosθ dθ = 2πIν ∫_{−1}^{1} μ dμ = 0,  μ = cosθ
Flux of Isotropic Radiation • Outward flux: Fν⁺ = ∫_0^{2π} ∫_0^{π/2} Iν cosθ sinθ dθ dφ = 2πIν ∫_0^1 μ dμ = πIν
Flux of Isotropic Radiation • Inward flux: Fν⁻ = −∫_0^{2π} ∫_{π/2}^{π} Iν cosθ sinθ dθ dφ = 2πIν ∫_0^{−1} μ dμ = πIν
Black-body Flux at Distance d • At the surface of a star: Fν,surf = πBν – Bν is the Planck function. [그림: 반지름 R인 구(별)와 거리 d 떨어진 점에서 별 가장자리에 접하는 원뿔, 반각 θs, 입체각 Ωs]
• At a distance d from the star: Fν,d = ∫_0^{2π} ∫_0^{θs} Bν cosθ sinθ dθ dφ = 2πBν ∫_{μs}^1 μ dμ = πBν(1 − μs²) = πBν sin²θs = πBν (R/d)² ≈ Bν ΔΩs
where ΔΩs is the solid angle subtended by the source: ΔΩs = ∫_0^{2π} ∫_0^{θs} dΩ = 2π(1 − cosθs) ≈ πθs² = π(R/d)²
• Luminosity: Lν = 4πR²Fν,surf = 4πR²πBν = 4πd²Fν,d
Radiation Pressure: Pν = (1/c) ∫ Iν cos²θ dΩ
• At a distance d from a star, Pν = (2π/c)Bν ∫_0^{θs} cos²θ sinθ dθ = (2π/c)Bν ∫_{μs}^1 μ² dμ = (2π/3c)Bν(1 − cos³θs) = (2π/3c)Bν·(3/2)θs² = (π/c)Bν(R/d)² = (1/c)Fν,d [그림: 슬라이드 5와 같은 별–원뿔 그림]

Radiation Force by Absorption • Define the flux vector of radiation propagating in the k̂-direction: 𝐅ν ≡ ∫ Iν k̂ dΩ – κν𝐅ν = absorbed flux per unit length (per unit frequency) = energy absorbed per unit volume per unit time (per unit frequency)
• Since p = E/c for photons, κν𝐅ν/c = the momentum absorbed per unit volume per unit time (per unit frequency) = the radiation force per unit volume (per unit frequency)
• Therefore, the total radiation force per unit volume is 𝐅rad = (1/c) ∫ κν𝐅ν dν
• Or, the total radiation force per unit mass is 𝐟 = (1/cρ) ∫ κν𝐅ν dν = (1/c) ∬ κ′ν Iν k̂ dν dΩ,  κ′ν = κν/ρ : opacity

Radiation Force vs. Pressure: dPrad/ds = Frad ⇒ Prad = ∫ Frad ds • Consider a slab with optical depth τν. • When Fν(0) is incident on the slab, Fν(s) = Fν(0)e^{−τ′ν} [그림: 초록색 슬랩, 왼쪽에서 Fν(0) 입사, 왼쪽 면 τν·오른쪽 면 0, s는 오른쪽으로 증가, dτ′ν = −κν ds]
• Since ∫ Frad ds = (1/c)∬ κνFν dν ds = (1/c)∬ κνFν(0)e^{−τ′ν} dν ds = (−1/c)∬ Fν(0)e^{−τ′ν} dν dτ′ν = (1/c)∫ Fν(0)(1 − e^{−τν}) dν (빨간색 강조: κν ds → −dτ′ν)

one obtains Prad ≅ F(0)/c in the limit of τν→∞. • This is equal to the expression for Prad at distance d from a star. – Prad corresponds to the radiation pressure when radiation is completely absorbed.

Q1 • Using the Sun’s luminosity and radius, calculate its (frequency-integrated) specific intensity. L⊙ = 3.85 × 10³³ erg s⁻¹, R⊙ = 6.96 × 10¹⁰ cm
Q1 • Answers: F⊙ = L⊙/(4πR⊙²) = 6.33 × 10¹⁰ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻²;  I⊙ = F⊙/π ≈ 2.0 × 10¹⁰ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² sr⁻¹

Q2 • Assuming that the only important source of light is the Sun, compute the (frequency-integrated) mean intensity and the energy density at the distance of Mars. I⊙ = 2 × 10¹⁰ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² sr⁻¹, R⊙ = 7 × 10¹⁰ cm, and rMars = 2.28 × 10¹³ cm (mean intensity, energy density 빨간색)
Q2 • Answers: J = 4.6 × 10⁴ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² sr⁻¹;  u = (4π/c)J = 2 × 10⁻⁵ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻³
note: python 재계산 J=4.71×10⁴(슬라이드 4.6×10⁴), u=1.98×10⁻⁵ erg cm⁻³ — 슬라이드 u 단위의 s⁻¹은 오타(에너지밀도는 erg cm⁻³)

raw: Q3 • Where does the Solar System end? There are different ways of defining the ‘edge’ of the Solar System, but suppose we take it to be the distance at which the radiation energy density from the Sun is equivalent to the ambient mean energy density of interstellar space, the latter about 10⁻¹² erg cm⁻³. • Calculate the radius of the solar system.
Q3 • Answer: r = √(πI⊙R⊙²/(uc)) = 1.0 × 10¹⁷ cm = 6700 au
Q4 • Find the relation between the radiation pressure Pν and energy density uν for isotropic radiation (as in the cosmic microwave radiation — 빨간색).
Q4 • Answer: Pν = (1/3)uν
